bible_daily.label: Bible & daily reading
bible_daily.placeholder: Ask about today's reading, reflection, or a passage…

statements.text: You're just starting — that's great. A little reading each day adds up.
Daily Bible reading builds a habit: choose a time and place, and start with a short passage.
Reflect after reading: What stood out? How does this apply to today?
You can follow a reading plan (e.g. chronological, thematic) or read one book at a time.
Journal a verse or thought from the passage to remember and apply it.
Prayer and reading go together: pray before for focus, after for application.
Start small: even a few verses daily is better than long sessions rarely.
Reflection prompts: What is God saying here? What should I do differently? What am I grateful for?
Use a study Bible or commentary for difficult passages; look up key terms if needed.

journaling.label: Journaling & ideas
journaling.placeholder: Ask about prompts, structure, or ideas…

statements.text: Journaling is writing for yourself: capture thoughts, ideas, and reflections without judgment.
Junk journaling combines writing with mixed media: use scraps, stickers, and collage to organize ideas and memories.
Freewriting means writing continuously for a set time without editing; it helps surface ideas.
Morning pages: write three pages by hand each morning to clear your head and uncover what matters.
Use prompts to get started: What am I avoiding? What went well today? What do I want to remember?
Organize ideas by theme: give each project or topic a section or tag so you can find it later.
Bullet journaling uses rapid logging: short bullets, signifiers, and collections to track tasks and thoughts.
Reflection prompts: What did I learn? What would I do differently? What am I grateful for?
Your journal is private; write for yourself first. Consistency matters more than length.
Capture ideas as they come: keep a running list or voice note, then expand in your journal later.

hiking.label: Hiking & outdoors
hiking.placeholder: Ask about gear, trails, or safety…

statements.text: Before a hike: check weather, tell someone your route and return time, and bring water and a first-aid kit.
Leave No Trace: pack out trash, stay on the trail, and minimize impact on plants and wildlife.
Day hike essentials: water, snacks, map or GPS, sun protection, extra layer, and a headlamp or light.
Trail difficulty is often rated by distance, elevation gain, and terrain; match the trail to your fitness.
Start early to avoid heat and afternoon storms; turn back if conditions worsen.
Break in new boots before a long hike to prevent blisters; bring blister treatment just in case.
Hydration: drink before you're thirsty; electrolytes help on long or hot hikes.
If you get lost: stop, stay put if possible, use whistle or signal; three of anything is a distress signal.

yoga.label: Yoga & practice
yoga.placeholder: Ask about poses, breathwork, or a short sequence…

statements.text: Start with a few minutes of breath awareness or gentle movement to arrive on the mat.
Warm up the body before deeper poses; listen to your body and skip or modify as needed.
Breathwork: try equal inhale and exhale, or extended exhale, to calm the nervous system.
A short daily practice (10–15 minutes) is more sustainable than long sessions rarely.
Common poses for beginners: Mountain, Down Dog, Child's pose, Cat-Cow, Warrior I.
Savasana at the end: lie still and let the body absorb the practice.
Yoga is not about flexibility; it is about awareness, breath, and gradual progress.

gardening.label: Gardening & plants
gardening.placeholder: Ask about plants, soil, sun, or experiments…
default_action_queries: Suggest 1–2 experiments or next steps based on my goals and what I've tried.

statements.text: You're just starting — that's great. Small steps build lasting habits; every plant you try teaches you something.
A low-maintenance urban garden focuses on hardy plants, good soil, and consistent but minimal care.
Match plants to light: note sun direction and hours; many herbs and greens do well in part sun.
Water consistently but avoid overwatering; let soil dry slightly between waterings for most plants.
Try one new plant or spot per season so you can learn what works in your space.
Track what works: note sun, water, and failures so you can adapt. Suggest one small experiment at a time; track result and adjust.
Containers and raised beds suit balconies and small spaces; use quality potting mix and drainage.
You're building real skills. Keep experimenting — your garden will reflect what you learn.
Suggest 1–2 small experiments based on the user's goal and constraints; then they can record outcomes.

home_brewing.label: Home brewing
home_brewing.placeholder: Ask about recipes, sanitation, or experiments…
default_action_queries: Suggest 1–2 experiments or next steps based on my goals and what I've tried.

statements.text: Sanitation is critical: clean and sanitize all equipment before use to avoid off flavors and infection.
Start with a simple recipe (e.g. single-malt, one hop) to learn the process before varying.
Good experiments: try one variable per batch (e.g. hop timing, yeast, temperature) and note results.
Suggest one small experiment at a time; track result and adjust. Record what worked and what didn't.
Fermentation temperature affects flavor; keep consistent and record it for each batch.
Take notes on each batch: recipe, dates, temps, and tasting notes so you can repeat or improve.

music_production.label: Music production
music_production.placeholder: Ask about workflow, techniques, or experiments…
default_action_queries: Suggest 1–2 experiments or next steps based on my goals and what I've tried.

statements.text: A lo-fi beats producer often uses sampled drums, warm keys, and tape-style saturation for a relaxed feel.
Workflow: start with a loop or sketch, then build structure; finish one track before piling on new ideas.
Experiments: try one new technique per track (e.g. sidechain, filter sweep); note what fits your style.
Suggest one small experiment at a time; track result and adjust. Record what worked and what didn't.
Reference tracks: compare your mix to songs you like; note levels, width, and balance.
Export and listen on different devices and environments to catch mix issues early.

birdwatching.label: Birdwatching
birdwatching.placeholder: Ask about species, checklists, or seasonal tips…
default_action_queries: Suggest 1–2 experiments or next steps based on my goals and what I've tried.

statements.text: You're just starting — that's great. Small steps build lasting habits; enjoy the journey.
Get started with a field guide or app; learn a few common species in your area first.
Keep a checklist or log: species, date, location, and conditions help you see patterns over time.
Migration seasons bring new species; note when and where you see them to learn seasonal patterns.
Track sightings and conditions; note patterns over seasons. Suggest one small experiment (e.g. new spot, time of day) and record results.
Binoculars and quiet observation: move slowly, avoid startling birds, and note behavior and habitat.
You're building real skills. Keep going — your checklist and notes will reward you over time.
Suggest 1–2 small experiments based on the user's goal (e.g. new location, checklist goal); then they can record outcomes.
You're taking a good step. Small progress is still progress.
Set a clear goal for what you want to achieve; write it down so you can refer back.
Break large tasks into smaller steps; tackle one step at a time.
Review and refine your goals periodically; adjust as you learn what works for you.
